item.title: CK Hutchison begins arbitration against Panama over annulled canal contract
item.description: Hong Kong-based conglomerate CK Hutchison said in a statement Tuesday it has initiated international arbitration against Panama, after a ruling by the country’s top court annulled a concession allowing it to operate ports at the Panama Canal. item.title: Exclusive: Police say ‘drone in operation’ warnings to remain up in communities, even when patrols not taking place
item.description: Warning banners reading “Police Drone in Operation” will remain up in local communities, even when there is no aerial surveillance operation taking place, police have confirmed to HKFP. Last month, the Hong Kong Police Force (HKPF) announced they would expand the use of drones for crime prevention to areas including The Peak, Cheung Chau and […]

item.title: Greenpeace warns 22 gov’t-promoted ‘eco-tourism’ sites lack statutory protection, as festive holiday nears
item.description: Twenty-two “eco-tourism” hotspots promoted by the government are not protected by the city’s environmental statutes, a green group warned on Wednesday, calling on the authorities to prevent overtourism at local natural attractions. Greenpeace campaigner Ha Shun-kuen on Wednesday told a radio programme that at least 22 sites with high ecological value in Hong Kong are […]

item.title: Rights group decries detention of Chinese investigative journalists Liu Hu and Wu Yingjiao
item.description: Rights group Reporters Without Borders condemned on Tuesday the detention of a prominent Chinese investigative journalist after he published an article alleging corruption among local officials. Liu Hu became widely known more than 10 years ago for his reports on graft among high-profile figures in the Chinese Communist Party and government. Police in the southwestern […]

item.title: Public health is part of national security, police officer tells trial of Hong Kong Tiananmen vigil activists
item.description: A Hong Kong police officer testifying at the national security trial of two Tiananmen vigil activists has said that she opposed the candlelight commemorative gathering in June 2020 out of public health concerns. item.title: Hong Kong man gets 80 hours community service for tearing off ‘fingertip’-sized corner of election poster
item.description: A Hong Kong man who tore off the corner of a poster promoting last year’s “patriots only” legislative elections has been sentenced to 80 hours of community service, after pleading guilty to damaging the promotional material “for fun”. Mo Chi-kit, 23, was sentenced on Wednesday at the West Kowloon Magistrates’ Courts by Principal Magistrate Don […]

item.title: Exclusive: Hong Kong declines to confirm if formerly sanctioned UK MPs can enter city, after PM says China travel ban lifted
item.description: China has lifted “all restrictions” on six sanctioned British parliamentarians, UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer has said after talks last week with President Xi Jinping. item.title: Event: Shi Fu Miz Festival 2026 – line-up and peek at the new eco-park venue
item.description: Shi Fu Miz Festival is returning next month for a new edition at Tai Tong Ecopark in Yuen Long. item.title: Panama hits back after China warns of ‘heavy price’ in ports dispute
item.description: Panama’s President Jose Raul Mulino on Wednesday rejected China’s threat to make the Central American country pay a “heavy price” after a Hong Kong company was evicted from two ports on the Panama Canal.
